column1: # Pre-registered manifest — orchestrate-loop GENERALIZATION arm. Written BEFORE
# the first cell. Separate arm, separate results file.
# WHY. Block A's 27/29 = 93% was measured on ONE task: the `roadmap` spec, one
# synthetic FastAPI app, one 13-test oracle. Thirty seeds on one task measures
# seed variance, not task variance — and the /goal v5 finding (a byte-identical
# prompt swinging 2/3 -> 0/3 at fixed seed) is a standing warning that
# task-to-task variance is plausibly larger than what a seed sweep can see. A
# rate on one task cannot be generalized to "the loop", and this campaign has
# not yet tested that it does. This is the single highest-value remaining
# question, cheaper than any further Mellum n.
# THE SECOND TASK. `roadmap-user-story` (fixtures/agenttest/specs/roadmap-user-story.md,
# 82 lines vs roadmap.md's 56): the identical target app — same routes, same
# redirect contract, same data model, same 13-test acceptance suite — but
# phrased as user-facing business outcomes rather than implementation
# instructions. Genuinely different task SHAPE (the orchestrator must derive
# the same file/phase plan from a differently-organized spec), same oracle, so
# a rate difference is attributable to task framing rather than a harder grader.
# `writableFiles` in main.swift is not spec-conditional and is correct for both
# specs (confirmed by reading both spec files against it). Never run through
# the directive path before this arm (checked: no prior
# captures/agenttest/*-roadmap-user-story-directive dirs).
# PROVENANCE: repo HEAD f61de85 + uncommitted main.swift (repairEmissionFollowUp
# switch — inert on this path, directive mode never calls RepairLoop). ds4 pin
# 1a2dddf. Same configuration as Block A's main pass: laguna-s-2.1, think budget
# 1500, 2-worker pool, 4-round cap. TURN_TIMEOUT=1500 (between the main pass's
# 900s, which truncated a genuine multi-dispatch tail, and the long-turn arm's
# 1800s) so this arm does not repeat that mistake at 1/3 the n.
# DESIGN: n=10, seeds 201-210 — disjoint from every prior seed on the directive
# path (42, 101-130). n=10 is deliberately small: this is a SCREEN for a large
# generalization failure, not a precision instrument. Wilson width at n=10 is
# wide by design; see the decision rule below for what that width can and
# cannot support.
# PRIMARY ENDPOINT: pass rate on roadmap-user-story, reported with its Wilson
# interval, read AGAINST Block A's 27/29 = 93% baseline — not pooled with it
# (different task; pooling would average two different quantities, the same
# mistake the depth-2/depth-3 pooling made).
# DECISION RULE, fixed before the first cell:
#  1. >=8/10 (80%): the loop generalizes across this task shift; no further
#     action needed on genericity grounds alone.
#  2. 5-7/10: a real signal that task framing matters, underpowered to size it.
#     Next step is a larger arm on this same spec, not a different spec.
#  3. <=4/10: the loop's reliability is task-specific, not a property of the
#     loop; the 93% figure must not be quoted without the caveat "measured on
#     one task" from here forward, and the failure captures become P27 inputs
#     directly (same taxonomy discipline as the roadmap voids).
# Every non-pass cell gets read for its failure mode, same as the roadmap
# arm's seed-106 (dispatch-ordering deadlock) and seed-109 (malformed tool call
# in think) — those two roadmap-backlog entries are candidates a second task
# might reproduce or might not; either answer is informative.
# WHAT THIS CANNOT CONCLUDE: a precise rate on this task (n=10 gives a wide
# interval by design); anything about tasks other than these two.
# Runner: TURN_TIMEOUT=1500 RUN_CAP=3600 \
#   CAMPAIGN_MANIFEST=<this> \
